title: Factory move A: foundation — credentials, gatewaytrace, contract packages, shared plumbing
description:
Foundation for the factory move: Go only, no embedded payload, no CLI wiring.
Everything downstream depends on the two decisions made here.

Accepted from tick v3i's blocked report, which read the real source rather than
trusting the epic's prose and found two things the description had wrong.

Move into ticfac's internal/factory tree, with import-path rewrites:
- internal/factory/credentials (reads/writes ~/.ticfacrc)
- internal/gatewaytrace — NOT in the original list. internal/factory/dashboard
  imports it in production code; it depends only on credentials, which is
  moving, so it is a clean addition.
- internal/factory/{jobprotocol,lifecycle,runstate}
- internal/factory's shared plumbing: bundle.go, sourceref.go, token.go,
  deviceflow.go, githubapp.go, tkcommands.go, billing.go

Reimplement the contract-parity tests: those packages' contract_test.go and
evidence_cross_contract_test.go import ticks' internal/tkcontract, which CANNOT
move — cmd/tk's own version and root contract gate use it. ticfac already has
the equivalent: internal/schema, which internal/tk uses for the same
tk-json-manifest.json validation. Reimplement against that, do not copy
tkcontract.

The contract fixtures those packages read by relative path
(../../../contracts/{job-protocol,ticfac-run-state,credential-ownership,collect-vocabulary}.json)
already exist byte-identical in ticfac's pinned contracts/, so the relative path
resolves after the move with no rewrite. ticfac's internal/contracts/parity has
its OWN independent readers for the same contracts; that is the deliberate
no-shared-code pattern this codebase uses, not a collision. Both coexist.

TWO DECISIONS, already made by the epic owner — implement them, and say in your
RESULT file if the code makes either look wrong:

1. HasCommand (the required-tk-commands gate). tkcommands.go regex-scans the
   embedded entrypoints for `tk <sub>` and asks a caller-supplied predicate
   whether the binary implements them. After the move ticfac does not ship tk,
   so there is no cobra tree to ask. DECISION: drop the fast preflight and rely
   on the Dockerfile-embedded check, which runs against the tk that will
   ACTUALLY be in the image. Shelling out to `tk` on PATH would test a
   different binary from the one that runs — a false signal is worse than a
   late one. If a fast check is wanted later it must run against the pinned
   ticks ref, never PATH.
2. SourceRef / version pin: which ticks ref `ticfac factory deploy` builds the
   sandbox's tk from. It is NOT contracts.pin.json's ref, which is scoped
   differently and moves independently per its own doc comment. DECISION: an
   explicit repo-level pin, reviewable and version-controlled — not a field in
   the per-operator ~/.ticfacrc and not a bare flag, because which ticks built
   the sandbox is a property of the deployment that a reviewer must be able to
   see in a diff. Choose the exact file and shape and say why.

Builds and tests green as a LIBRARY. No cmd/ticfac wiring in this tick.
acceptance_criteria: credentials, gatewaytrace, jobprotocol, lifecycle, runstate and the shared plumbing build and test inside ticfac with no import of any ticks package; the contract-parity tests are reimplemented against internal/schema rather than a copy of tkcontract; the relative-path contract fixtures still resolve; the required-tk-commands gate relies on the Dockerfile-embedded check with the reasoning recorded; the ticks source ref is pinned in a reviewable repo-level file whose shape and rationale are stated; no cmd wiring lands here; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green (make test-short).
